items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: speaking of McKinney's Cotton Pickers, Fletcher Henderson... they played dances.

ctx.x: You know, Danny, during those years singers were the principals. You don't think that Coleman Hawkins could take his tenor saxophone player and go out and stand in front of Butter-Beans and Susie and be the star. He was just another musician in the background. Maybe they'd let him play a number. Maybe. Or he'd have an opportunity when they did have an

opportunity to play was when the chorus girls...you know, you could really do your thing and play as hard as you wanted to which would be an inspiration to the chorus girls. But other than that they didn't have, you know, very seldom would you have a band that was the attraction. I can't even remember when they ever did that on the TOBA. And it's quite possible, but I'm telling you from my knowledge what they would do. They would...a guy would come on the show...he could play when the chorus girls were dancing,…

Clouds of Joy, Andy Kirk, you know, these guys were the Territory Bands that really, you know, played, but you very rarely saw Duke Ellington in Dallas, you know, during that period. He may play New York or Chicago or the Cotton Club or something and then go to California to Sebastian's or something like that. And then in 1927, when the Regal Theater opened, you know what I mean, they'd have a show. But they always had to have that original TOBA format of a comedian, Pigmeat Markham, you know what I mean,…
